title: 50agents vs Softr: apps for your team or clients | 50agents
description: Softr builds client portals and internal tools on your own domain; 50agents builds team apps run by AI agents from plain words. Every row sourced.
answer: Pick Softr if you need a client portal or an app for people outside your team, on your own domain, laid out in a visual editor.
Pick 50agents if the app is for your own team and you want AI agents to work its records for you, built from plain words; both start free.
ask: Keep track of customer requests and draft the replies
lede: Softr is the better app builder in the usual sense: portals, custom domains, client users and a visual editor you can use without AI.

us: The app is for your team, and you want AI agents doing the follow-up work inside it.
You want the app, its automations and its AI agents from plain words.
You would rather not lay out pages.
them: Clients or partners need to log in to it.
You need your own domain and your branding.
You want to design each page yourself in a visual editor.

move.title: Download your tables
move.body: Softr table data downloads as CSV or XLSX.

move.title: Ask for the app, then bring the data in
move.body: Tell Captain what the app is for. Once it is built, drop the CSV into the app's list, and Captain matches the columns to fields.

move.title: Keep Softr for anything client-facing
move.body: 50agents apps are for your workspace; keep portals where they are.

faqs.q: Can I build a client portal with 50agents?
faqs.a: No. 50agents apps are for the people in your workspace. Softr is built for portals.

faqs.q: Do both build apps from a prompt?
faqs.a: Yes. Softr's AI Co-Builder makes and changes apps from plain language; Captain builds 50agents apps from plain words and asks what it needs to know.
Both start free; check Softr's pricing page for its current plan limits. 50agents is free to start, and its apps are for your own team.
